evidenceRecords.population: 23 patients with previously treated metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC
evidenceRecords.finding: The 23-person trial found 67% versus 29% progression-free at three months (p=0.11); the small, prematurely closed study leaves substantial uncertainty.
evidenceRecords.limits: Small trial stopped early; the three-month progression-free difference was not statistically significant.

evidenceRecords.comparison: Itraconazole plus multidrug chemotherapy; no concurrent control
evidenceRecords.finding: The 38-patient retrospective series used itraconazole with docetaxel, gemcitabine and carboplatin; observed responses cannot be attributed to itraconazole alone.
evidenceRecords.limits: No concurrent comparison; the contribution of itraconazole cannot be isolated.

evidenceRecords.comparison: Temozolomide plus mebendazole versus lomustine plus mebendazole
evidenceRecords.finding: Nine-month survival was 36.6% with temozolomide–mebendazole and 45% with lomustine–mebendazole, below the 55% benchmark; both arms included mebendazole.
evidenceRecords.limits: Both groups received mebendazole; neither reached the prespecified 55% nine-month survival benchmark.

evidenceRecords.finding: The single-arm 36-patient study reported 66% progression-free at six months but concluded that improvement was not demonstrated.
evidenceRecords.limits: Single-arm study; the reported progression-free proportion does not establish improvement over chemoradiation alone.

evidenceRecords.population: 50 patients enrolled with invasive breast cancer
evidenceRecords.finding: Overall Ki-67 decreased by 7.6% (p=0.39); a larger decrease in the HMGCR-positive subgroup was exploratory and not a survival result.
evidenceRecords.limits: Two-week uncontrolled presurgical study; Ki-67 is a proliferation biomarker, not recurrence or survival.

effects.endpoint: Ki67 relative change in HMGCR-positive subgroup

evidenceRecords.comparison: Celecoxib versus placebo after primary breast-cancer treatment
evidenceRecords.finding: REACT found no disease-free survival advantage: hazard ratio 0.97 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.17).
evidenceRecords.limits: Disease-free survival was not improved; the estimate applies to the REACT trial population.

evidenceRecords.population: Resected stage III colon cancer receiving adjuvant chemotherapy
evidenceRecords.comparison: Celecoxib versus placebo alongside adjuvant chemotherapy
evidenceRecords.finding: Overall disease-free survival was not significantly improved (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.03); a preplanned PIK3CA subgroup analysis reported a more favorable result.
evidenceRecords.magnitude: Hazard ratio: 0.89 ratio (95% CI 0.76 to 1.03); p=0.12
evidenceRecords.limits: Overall disease-free survival was not significantly improved. The PIK3CA subgroup analysis comes from the same study family.

evidenceRecords.comparison: TACE plus celecoxib and lanreotide versus TACE
evidenceRecords.finding: Median survival was 15 months with TACE plus celecoxib and lanreotide versus 7.5 months with TACE alone; adding two drugs prevents assigning the benefit to celecoxib alone.
evidenceRecords.limits: Pilot trial adding two drugs; the survival difference cannot be assigned to celecoxib alone.

evidenceRecords.finding: Six weeks of adjunctive minocycline did not significantly improve depression severity versus placebo in the 168-person analysis.
evidenceRecords.magnitude: Between-group difference: 1.46 MADRS points (95% CI -1.04 to 3.96); p=0.25
evidenceRecords.limits: Six-week adjunctive-treatment trial; the confidence interval includes no difference.

evidenceRecords.population: 142 people after a first demyelinating event
evidenceRecords.comparison: Minocycline versus placebo after a first demyelinating event
evidenceRecords.finding: After a first demyelinating event, adjusted six-month conversion risk was 18.5 percentage points lower (95% CI 3.7 to 33.3); the 24-month difference was not significant.
evidenceRecords.magnitude: Adjusted absolute risk reduction: 18.5 percentage points (95% CI 3.7 to 33.3); p=0.01
evidenceRecords.limits: The adjusted six-month difference favored minocycline; the 24-month difference was not statistically significant.
